Company Profile: Reliance Industries Limited (NSE/BSE: RELIANCE)
Business Overview: Reliance Industries Limited (RIL) is India's largest corporate conglomerate by market capitalization and revenue. Operates market-leading businesses across Oil-to-Chemicals (O2C refining & petrochemicals), Retail (Reliance Retail), Digital Services (Jio Platforms), and New Energy (solar, hydrogen, energy storage gigafactories in Jamnagar).
Core Operating Segments: 1. Oil-to-Chemicals (O2C): Jamnagar complex with 1.24 million barrels/day refining capacity; 2. Digital Services (Jio): 490M+ subscribers, world's largest 5G standalone network, ARPU INR 195.1; 3. Reliance Retail: 18,900+ stores with INR 75,000+ Cr quarterly gross revenue; 4. Oil & Gas E&P: KG D6 deepwater gas producing 30 MMSCMD (accounting for ~30% of India's domestic gas production).
Key Financial Highlights: Consolidated Q2 FY25 revenue at INR 2,35,481 Cr, quarterly EBITDA at INR 43,934 Cr, and PAT at INR 19,323 Cr. Shareholders' net worth exceeds INR 7,94,900 Cr. Net debt to EBITDA remains prudent at ~0.65x. Approved 1:1 bonus equity share issue in October 2024, expanding retail investor base.
Regulatory & Tax Considerations: Regulated under Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board (PNGRB) pricing formulas for KG-D6 gas, Department of Telecommunications (DoT) spectrum usage charges and license fees, and Ministry of Finance windfall profit taxes on fuel exports.
Strategic Capex & Growth Catalysts: INR 75,000 Cr committed capex in Dhirubhai Ambani Green Energy Giga Complex (solar PV, energy storage, green hydrogen electrolysers). Accelerating 5G monetization, enterprise cloud partnerships with NVIDIA/Google, and planned value-unlocking listings of Jio and Retail.

<UNTRUSTED_STATUTORY_DOCUMENT id="FINANCE-ACT-2024-STT-DELIVERY" authority="Ministry of Finance, Government of India">
Finance (No. 2) Act 2024: Securities Transaction Tax (STT) Equity Delivery
Finance (No. 2) Act 2024, Chapter VII — Securities Transaction Tax: Under Section 98 and Section 99, taxable securities transactions in Equity Delivery on recognized stock exchanges shall be levied at 0.1% (one-tenth of one percent) payable by both the purchaser and seller. For equity intraday (non-delivery) transactions, the statutory rate is 0.025% payable by the seller only. Statutory costs are mandatory and deduct from gross trading turnover before net trading realization.
</UNTRUSTED_STATUTORY_DOCUMENT>

<UNTRUSTED_STATUTORY_DOCUMENT id="FINANCE-ACT-2024-STT-DERIVATIVES" authority="Ministry of Finance, Government of India">
Finance (No. 2) Act 2024: Revised STT on Futures and Options
Finance (No. 2) Act 2024, Section 98 Amendments effective October 1, 2024: 1. Sale of an option in securities: STT increased to 0.1% (from 0.0625%) of the option premium payable by seller. 2. Sale of a future in securities: STT increased to 0.02% (from 0.0125%) of the trade value payable by seller. Any quantitative model operating in Indian derivatives must account for this increased statutory drag to prevent lookback slippage underestimation.
</UNTRUSTED_STATUTORY_DOCUMENT>

retrieved_evidence.title: Finance (No. 2) Act 2024: Capital Gains Restructuring (12.5% LTCG & 20% STCG)
retrieved_evidence.sanitized_snippet:
<UNTRUSTED_STATUTORY_DOCUMENT id="FINANCE-ACT-2024-CAPITAL-GAINS" authority="Ministry of Finance, Government of India">
Finance (No. 2) Act 2024: Capital Gains Restructuring (12.5% LTCG & 20% STCG)
Finance (No. 2) Act 2024, Chapter IV amendments to Section 112A and Section 111A of the Income-tax Act, 1961: 1. Long-Term Capital Gains (LTCG) on listed equity shares, equity-oriented units, and business trust units held > 12 months are taxed at 12.5% (increased from 10%) for transfers on or after July 23, 2024. The annual aggregate LTCG exemption limit under Section 112A was increased from INR 1,00,000 to INR 1,25,000. 2. Short-Term Capital Gains (STCG) under Section 111A on listed equities held <= 12 months are taxed at 20% (increased from 15%). Indexation benefit on unlisted assets and real estate is rationalized to 12.5% without indexation.
</UNTRUSTED_STATUTORY_DOCUMENT>

<UNTRUSTED_STATUTORY_DOCUMENT id="SEBI-LODR-REG30-MATERIALITY" authority="Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)">
SEBI LODR Regulation 30: Disclosure of Material Events
SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 — Regulation 30: Every listed entity shall promptly make disclosures of any events or information which, in the opinion of the board of directors, are material. Material events under Schedule III Part A must be disclosed to recognized stock exchanges (NSE/BSE) as soon as reasonably possible and no later than: (a) thirty minutes from the closure of the board meeting for outcome disclosures; (b) twelve hours from occurrence for events originating within the entity; (c) twenty-four hours from occurrence for external events.
</UNTRUSTED_STATUTORY_DOCUMENT>

Finance (No. 2) Act 2024, Chapter VII — Securities Transaction Tax: Under Section 98 and Section 99, taxable securities transactions in Equity Delivery on recognized stock exchanges shall be levied at 0.1% (one-tenth of one percent) payable by both the purchaser and seller. Take rate stands at 23.5%-24.0% with positive contribution margin of ~6.8% of GOV. 2. Quick Commerce (Instamart): Rapidly scaling dark-store network with 605+ active dark stores across 43 Indian cities. Instamart GOV reached INR 8,500+ Cr annualized growing 86% YoY. Average order value (AOV) is INR 485. 3. Out-of-Home & Supply Chain: Dineout restaurant reservations & table payments, plus Scootsy warehouse operations.

Regulatory & Tax Considerations: Subject to SEBI LODR quarterly reporting obligations, DPIIT Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) ecommerce marketplace guidelines, and state-level gig worker welfare legislation (Karnataka, Rajasthan Gig Worker welfare boards). No foreign direct ownership of grocery inventory (strictly operates marketplace model with dark-store merchant partners).
Strategic Capex & Growth Catalysts: Planned Capex of INR 1,178 Cr from IPO proceeds for expanding Instamart dark store footprint from 605 to over 1,000 stores by FY26. retrieved_evidence.sanitized_snippet:
<UNTRUSTED_STATUTORY_DOCUMENT id="FINANCE-ACT-2024-STT-DELIVERY" authority="Ministry of Finance, Government of India">
Finance (No. 2) Act 2024: Securities Transaction Tax (STT) Equity Delivery
Finance (No. 2) Act 2024, Chapter VII — Securities Transaction Tax: Under Section 98 and Section 99, taxable securities transactions in Equity Delivery on recognized stock exchanges shall be levied at 0.1% (one-tenth of one percent) payable by both the purchaser and seller. For equity intraday (non-delivery) transactions, the statutory rate is 0.025% payable by the seller only. Statutory costs are mandatory and deduct from gross trading turnover before net trading realization.

retrieved_evidence.sanitized_snippet:
<UNTRUSTED_STATUTORY_DOCUMENT id="FINANCE-ACT-2024-STT-DELIVERY" authority="Ministry of Finance, Government of India">
Finance (No. 2) Act 2024: Securities Transaction Tax (STT) Equity Delivery
Finance (No. 2) Act 2024, Chapter VII — Securities Transaction Tax: Under Section 98 and Section 99, taxable securities transactions in Equity Delivery on recognized stock exchanges shall be levied at 0.1% (one-tenth of one percent) payable by both the purchaser and seller. For equity intraday (non-delivery) transactions, the statutory rate is 0.025% payable by the seller only. Statutory costs are mandatory and deduct from gross trading turnover before net trading realization.
</UNTRUSTED_STATUTORY_DOCUMENT>

<UNTRUSTED_STATUTORY_DOCUMENT id="FINANCE-ACT-2024-STT-DERIVATIVES" authority="Ministry of Finance, Government of India">
Finance (No. 2) Act 2024: Revised STT on Futures and Options
Finance (No. 2) Act 2024, Section 98 Amendments effective October 1, 2024: 1. Sale of an option in securities: STT increased to 0.1% (from 0.0625%) of the option premium payable by seller. 2. Sale of a future in securities: STT increased to 0.02% (from 0.0125%) of the trade value payable by seller. Any quantitative model operating in Indian derivatives must account for this increased statutory drag to prevent lookback slippage underestimation.

retrieved_evidence.title: Finance (No. 2) Act 2024: Capital Gains Restructuring (12.5% LTCG & 20% STCG)
retrieved_evidence.sanitized_snippet:
<UNTRUSTED_STATUTORY_DOCUMENT id="FINANCE-ACT-2024-CAPITAL-GAINS" authority="Ministry of Finance, Government of India">
Finance (No. 2) Act 2024: Capital Gains Restructuring (12.5% LTCG & 20% STCG)
Finance (No. 2) Act 2024, Chapter IV amendments to Section 112A and Section 111A of the Income-tax Act, 1961: 1. Long-Term Capital Gains (LTCG) on listed equity shares, equity-oriented units, and business trust units held > 12 months are taxed at 12.5% (increased from 10%) for transfers on or after July 23, 2024. The annual aggregate LTCG exemption limit under Section 112A was increased from INR 1,00,000 to INR 1,25,000. 2. Short-Term Capital Gains (STCG) under Section 111A on listed equities held <= 12 months are taxed at 20% (increased from 15%). Indexation benefit on unlisted assets and real estate is rationalized to 12.5% without indexation.
</UNTRUSTED_STATUTORY_DOCUMENT>

Finance (No. 2) Act 2024: Securities Transaction Tax (STT) Equity Delivery
Finance (No. 2) Act 2024, Chapter VII — Securities Transaction Tax: Under Section 98 and Section 99, taxable securities transactions in Equity Delivery on recognized stock exchanges shall be levied at 0.1% (one-tenth of one percent) payable by both the purchaser and seller. For equity intraday (non-delivery) transactions, the statutory rate is 0.025% payable by the seller only. Statutory costs are mandatory and deduct from gross trading turnover before net trading realization.

Company Profile: Swiggy Limited (NSE/BSE: SWIGGY)
Business Overview: Swiggy Limited is one of India's leading consumer tech on-demand convenience platforms. Pioneered hyper-local delivery in India with an integrated consumer ecosystem covering Food Delivery, Quick Commerce (Instamart), Out-of-Home consumption (Dineout), and on-demand delivery (Genie). Listed on NSE and BSE on November 13, 2024, successfully raising INR 11,327 crore in India's second-largest tech IPO of 2024.
Core Operating Segments: 1. Food Delivery: Gross Order Value (GOV) exceeding INR 24,000 Cr annualized with ~14M average monthly transacting users (MTUs). Take rate stands at 23.5%-24.0% with positive contribution margin of ~6.8% of GOV. 2. Quick Commerce (Instamart): Rapidly scaling dark-store network with 605+ active dark stores across 43 Indian cities. Instamart GOV reached INR 8,500+ Cr annualized growing 86% YoY. Average order value (AOV) is INR 485. 3. Out-of-Home & Supply Chain: Dineout restaurant reservations & table payments, plus Scootsy warehouse operations.
Key Financial Highlights: Consolidated quarterly revenue from operations reached INR 3,601.5 Cr in Q2 FY25. Post-IPO net worth stands at INR 9,250 Cr, bolstered by fresh issue proceeds. Cash and liquid investments exceed INR 5,800 Cr, ensuring a multi-year cash runway with zero net debt. Quick commerce adjusted EBITDA margin is approaching breakeven (-3.2% of GOV vs -8.9% YoY).
Regulatory & Tax Considerations: Subject to SEBI LODR quarterly reporting obligations, DPIIT Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) ecommerce marketplace guidelines, and state-level gig worker welfare legislation (Karnataka, Rajasthan Gig Worker welfare boards). No foreign direct ownership of grocery inventory (strictly operates marketplace model with dark-store merchant partners).
Strategic Capex & Growth Catalysts: Planned Capex of INR 1,178 Cr from IPO proceeds for expanding Instamart dark store footprint from 605 to over 1,000 stores by FY26. INR 703 Cr earmarked for supply chain infrastructure, cold storage, and dark store robotic automation. INR 1,115 Cr dedicated to technology and cloud infrastructure. Finance (No. 2) Act 2024: Revised STT on Futures and Options
Finance (No. 2) Act 2024, Section 98 Amendments effective October 1, 2024: 1. Sale of an option in securities: STT increased to 0.1% (from 0.0625%) of the option premium payable by seller. 2. Sale of a future in securities: STT increased to 0.02% (from 0.0125%) of the trade value payable by seller. retrieved_evidence.title: Finance (No. 2) Act 2024: Securities Transaction Tax (STT) Equity Delivery
retrieved_evidence.sanitized_snippet:
<UNTRUSTED_STATUTORY_DOCUMENT id="FINANCE-ACT-2024-STT-DELIVERY" authority="Ministry of Finance, Government of India">
Finance (No. 2) Act 2024: Securities Transaction Tax (STT) Equity Delivery
Finance (No. 2) Act 2024, Chapter VII — Securities Transaction Tax: Under Section 98 and Section 99, taxable securities transactions in Equity Delivery on recognized stock exchanges shall be levied at 0.1% (one-tenth of one percent) payable by both the purchaser and seller. For equity intraday (non-delivery) transactions, the statutory rate is 0.025% payable by the seller only. Statutory costs are mandatory and deduct from gross trading turnover before net trading realization.
</UNTRUSTED_STATUTORY_DOCUMENT>

retrieved_evidence.sanitized_snippet:
<UNTRUSTED_STATUTORY_DOCUMENT id="FINANCE-ACT-2024-STT-DERIVATIVES" authority="Ministry of Finance, Government of India">
Finance (No. 2) Act 2024: Revised STT on Futures and Options
Finance (No. 2) Act 2024, Section 98 Amendments effective October 1, 2024: 1. Sale of an option in securities: STT increased to 0.1% (from 0.0625%) of the option premium payable by seller. 2. Sale of a future in securities: STT increased to 0.02% (from 0.0125%) of the trade value payable by seller. Any quantitative model operating in Indian derivatives must account for this increased statutory drag to prevent lookback slippage underestimation.
</UNTRUSTED_STATUTORY_DOCUMENT>

retrieved_evidence.title: Finance (No. 2) Act 2024: Capital Gains Restructuring (12.5% LTCG & 20% STCG)
retrieved_evidence.sanitized_snippet:
<UNTRUSTED_STATUTORY_DOCUMENT id="FINANCE-ACT-2024-CAPITAL-GAINS" authority="Ministry of Finance, Government of India">
Finance (No. 2) Act 2024: Capital Gains Restructuring (12.5% LTCG & 20% STCG)
Finance (No. 2) Act 2024, Chapter IV amendments to Section 112A and Section 111A of the Income-tax Act, 1961: 1. Long-Term Capital Gains (LTCG) on listed equity shares, equity-oriented units, and business trust units held > 12 months are taxed at 12.5% (increased from 10%) for transfers on or after July 23, 2024. The annual aggregate LTCG exemption limit under Section 112A was increased from INR 1,00,000 to INR 1,25,000. 2. Short-Term Capital Gains (STCG) under Section 111A on listed equities held <= 12 months are taxed at 20% (increased from 15%). Indexation benefit on unlisted assets and real estate is rationalized to 12.5% without indexation.
</UNTRUSTED_STATUTORY_DOCUMENT>

Company Profile: Swiggy Limited (NSE/BSE: SWIGGY)
Business Overview: Swiggy Limited is one of India's leading consumer tech on-demand convenience platforms. Pioneered hyper-local delivery in India with an integrated consumer ecosystem covering Food Delivery, Quick Commerce (Instamart), Out-of-Home consumption (Dineout), and on-demand delivery (Genie). Listed on NSE and BSE on November 13, 2024, successfully raising INR 11,327 crore in India's second-largest tech IPO of 2024.
Core Operating Segments: 1. Food Delivery: Gross Order Value (GOV) exceeding INR 24,000 Cr annualized with ~14M average monthly transacting users (MTUs). Take rate stands at 23.5%-24.0% with positive contribution margin of ~6.8% of GOV. 2. Quick Commerce (Instamart): Rapidly scaling dark-store network with 605+ active dark stores across 43 Indian cities. Instamart GOV reached INR 8,500+ Cr annualized growing 86% YoY. Average order value (AOV) is INR 485. 3. Out-of-Home & Supply Chain: Dineout restaurant reservations & table payments, plus Scootsy warehouse operations.
Key Financial Highlights: Consolidated quarterly revenue from operations reached INR 3,601.5 Cr in Q2 FY25. Post-IPO net worth stands at INR 9,250 Cr, bolstered by fresh issue proceeds. Cash and liquid investments exceed INR 5,800 Cr, ensuring a multi-year cash runway with zero net debt. Quick commerce adjusted EBITDA margin is approaching breakeven (-3.2% of GOV vs -8.9% YoY).
Regulatory & Tax Considerations: Subject to SEBI LODR quarterly reporting obligations, DPIIT Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) ecommerce marketplace guidelines, and state-level gig worker welfare legislation (Karnataka, Rajasthan Gig Worker welfare boards). No foreign direct ownership of grocery inventory (strictly operates marketplace model with dark-store merchant partners).
Strategic Capex & Growth Catalysts: Planned Capex of INR 1,178 Cr from IPO proceeds for expanding Instamart dark store footprint from 605 to over 1,000 stores by FY26. retrieved_evidence.sanitized_snippet:
<UNTRUSTED_STATUTORY_DOCUMENT id="FINANCE-ACT-2024-STT-DELIVERY" authority="Ministry of Finance, Government of India">
Finance (No. 2) Act 2024: Securities Transaction Tax (STT) Equity Delivery
Finance (No. 2) Act 2024, Chapter VII — Securities Transaction Tax: Under Section 98 and Section 99, taxable securities transactions in Equity Delivery on recognized stock exchanges shall be levied at 0.1% (one-tenth of one percent) payable by both the purchaser and seller. For equity intraday (non-delivery) transactions, the statutory rate is 0.025% payable by the seller only. Statutory costs are mandatory and deduct from gross trading turnover before net trading realization.

Company Profile: Reliance Industries Limited (NSE/BSE: RELIANCE)
Business Overview: Reliance Industries Limited (RIL) is India's largest corporate conglomerate by market capitalization and revenue. Operates market-leading businesses across Oil-to-Chemicals (O2C refining & petrochemicals), Retail (Reliance Retail), Digital Services (Jio Platforms), and New Energy (solar, hydrogen, energy storage gigafactories in Jamnagar).
Core Operating Segments: 1. Oil-to-Chemicals (O2C): Jamnagar complex with 1.24 million barrels/day refining capacity; 2. Digital Services (Jio): 490M+ subscribers, world's largest 5G standalone network, ARPU INR 195.1; 3. Reliance Retail: 18,900+ stores with INR 75,000+ Cr quarterly gross revenue; 4. Oil & Gas E&P: KG D6 deepwater gas producing 30 MMSCMD (accounting for ~30% of India's domestic gas production).
Key Financial Highlights: Consolidated Q2 FY25 revenue at INR 2,35,481 Cr, quarterly EBITDA at INR 43,934 Cr, and PAT at INR 19,323 Cr. Shareholders' net worth exceeds INR 7,94,900 Cr. Regulatory & Tax Considerations: Regulated under Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board (PNGRB) pricing formulas for KG-D6 gas, Department of Telecommunications (DoT) spectrum usage charges and license fees, and Ministry of Finance windfall profit taxes on fuel exports.
Strategic Capex & Growth Catalysts: INR 75,000 Cr committed capex in Dhirubhai Ambani Green Energy Giga Complex (solar PV, energy storage, green hydrogen electrolysers). retrieved_evidence.title: Finance (No. 2) Act 2024: Securities Transaction Tax (STT) Equity Delivery
retrieved_evidence.sanitized_snippet:
<UNTRUSTED_STATUTORY_DOCUMENT id="FINANCE-ACT-2024-STT-DELIVERY" authority="Ministry of Finance, Government of India">
Finance (No. 2) Act 2024: Securities Transaction Tax (STT) Equity Delivery
Finance (No. 2) Act 2024, Chapter VII — Securities Transaction Tax: Under Section 98 and Section 99, taxable securities transactions in Equity Delivery on recognized stock exchanges shall be levied at 0.1% (one-tenth of one percent) payable by both the purchaser and seller. For equity intraday (non-delivery) transactions, the statutory rate is 0.025% payable by the seller only. Statutory costs are mandatory and deduct from gross trading turnover before net trading realization.
</UNTRUSTED_STATUTORY_DOCUMENT>

retrieved_evidence.title: Finance (No. 2) Act 2024: Revised STT on Futures and Options
retrieved_evidence.sanitized_snippet:
<UNTRUSTED_STATUTORY_DOCUMENT id="FINANCE-ACT-2024-STT-DERIVATIVES" authority="Ministry of Finance, Government of India">
Finance (No. 2) Act 2024: Revised STT on Futures and Options
Finance (No. 2) Act 2024, Section 98 Amendments effective October 1, 2024: 1. Sale of an option in securities: STT increased to 0.1% (from 0.0625%) of the option premium payable by seller. 2. Sale of a future in securities: STT increased to 0.02% (from 0.0125%) of the trade value payable by seller. Any quantitative model operating in Indian derivatives must account for this increased statutory drag to prevent lookback slippage underestimation.
</UNTRUSTED_STATUTORY_DOCUMENT>

retrieved_evidence.title: Finance (No. 2) Act 2024: Capital Gains Restructuring (12.5% LTCG & 20% STCG)
retrieved_evidence.sanitized_snippet:
<UNTRUSTED_STATUTORY_DOCUMENT id="FINANCE-ACT-2024-CAPITAL-GAINS" authority="Ministry of Finance, Government of India">
Finance (No. 2) Act 2024: Capital Gains Restructuring (12.5% LTCG & 20% STCG)
Finance (No. 2) Act 2024, Chapter IV amendments to Section 112A and Section 111A of the Income-tax Act, 1961: 1. Long-Term Capital Gains (LTCG) on listed equity shares, equity-oriented units, and business trust units held > 12 months are taxed at 12.5% (increased from 10%) for transfers on or after July 23, 2024. The annual aggregate LTCG exemption limit under Section 112A was increased from INR 1,00,000 to INR 1,25,000. 2. Short-Term Capital Gains (STCG) under Section 111A on listed equities held <= 12 months are taxed at 20% (increased from 15%). Indexation benefit on unlisted assets and real estate is rationalized to 12.5% without indexation.
</UNTRUSTED_STATUTORY_DOCUMENT>

SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 — Regulation 30: Every listed entity shall promptly make disclosures of any events or information which, in the opinion of the board of directors, are material. Material events under Schedule III Part A must be disclosed to recognized stock exchanges (NSE/BSE) as soon as reasonably possible and no later than: (a) thirty minutes from the closure of the board meeting for outcome disclosures; (b) twelve hours from occurrence for events originating within the entity; (c) twenty-four hours from occurrence for external events.

Company Profile: Swiggy Limited (NSE/BSE: SWIGGY)
Business Overview: Swiggy Limited is one of India's leading consumer tech on-demand convenience platforms. Listed on NSE and BSE on November 13, 2024, successfully raising INR 11,327 crore in India's second-largest tech IPO of 2024.
Core Operating Segments: 1. Food Delivery: Gross Order Value (GOV) exceeding INR 24,000 Cr annualized with ~14M average monthly transacting users (MTUs). Take rate stands at 23.5%-24.0% with positive contribution margin of ~6.8% of GOV. 2. Quick Commerce (Instamart): Rapidly scaling dark-store network with 605+ active dark stores across 43 Indian cities. Instamart GOV reached INR 8,500+ Cr annualized growing 86% YoY. Average order value (AOV) is INR 485. 3. Out-of-Home & Supply Chain: Dineout restaurant reservations & table payments, plus Scootsy warehouse operations.
Key Financial Highlights: Consolidated quarterly revenue from operations reached INR 3,601.5 Cr in Q2 FY25. Post-IPO net worth stands at INR 9,250 Cr, bolstered by fresh issue proceeds. Regulatory & Tax Considerations: Subject to SEBI LODR quarterly reporting obligations, DPIIT Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) ecommerce marketplace guidelines, and state-level gig worker welfare legislation (Karnataka, Rajasthan Gig Worker welfare boards). No foreign direct ownership of grocery inventory (strictly operates marketplace model with dark-store merchant partners).
Strategic Capex & Growth Catalysts: Planned Capex of INR 1,178 Cr from IPO proceeds for expanding Instamart dark store footprint from 605 to over 1,000 stores by FY26.
